evidence_tree.command: git archive --format=tar HEAD data docs/math-foundations.md | tar -x -C <fresh scratch>
evidence_tree.isolation: Only data/ and docs/math-foundations.md were read. src/, tests/, scripts/, docs/plans/, docs/receipts/, the diff, the plan, and git history were never opened.

sources.quote: Transcendent Bonus: Collecting 60 Splinters of Wrath enhances Force of Will to deal 12% (+ 2% per 100 AP) bonus true damage.

sources.note: The wiki labels the combined W output MIXED, not MAGIC. Mixed is only representable as at least one magic component plus at least one true component; the base recast damage stays magic.

sources.quote: Recast: Syndra throws the grabbed target towards the target location ... dealing magic damage to them and nearby enemies once they land.

sources.note: Ability-level scalar. It describes the recast nuke only and is the field a naive implementation would stamp onto every component of the W, which is exactly the shape of the observed old value.

sources.quote: All damage and splinter atom families covered: splinters option (0-120) gates Q2 second charge, W 60-splinter true-damage (12%+2%/100 AP), P 120-splinter +15% AP buff; R reads 'Magic Damage per Sphere' x user-set sphere count.
E3 implemented the Transcendent splinter system (splinters option: 120 -> 1.15x AP buff, 40+ Q charges via Q2 slot, 60+ W true damage), R sphere count (r_spheres).

sources.path: Syndra (whole record), regex scan for 'true damage'
sources.quote: Exactly two hits: the W Transcendent Bonus description and the 'Bonus True Damage' leveling attribute. Q, E, R and the passive contain no true-damage text; all four carry damageType MAGIC_DAMAGE.

No section assigns per-event damage types; the document covers penetration order, resistance, DoT partitioning and the survival walk. It neither supports nor contradicts this leaf, so the wiki cache is the sole authority here.

threshold_check.statement: 'Collecting 60 Splinters of Wrath' is inclusive at 60.
threshold_check.consequence: At the scenario's splinter value of 60 the Transcendent bonus is ACTIVE, so a true-damage component must be present in this fight. Scenario suffix '_60' pins exactly this threshold.

decomposition.claim: The Transcendent bonus is an ADDITIONAL true-damage instance equal to (12% + 2% per 100 AP) of the W recast's magic damage; the recast damage itself stays magic.

verification_against_cached_leveling_row.constant_term: 0.12 * base = [8.4, 12.0, 15.6, 19.2, 22.8]  -> matches cached flat_by_rank EXACTLY for all 5 ranks
verification_against_cached_leveling_row.linear_ap_term: (0.12 * 0.65 + 0.0002 * base) * 100 = [9.2, 9.8, 10.4, 11.0, 11.6] %AP  -> matches cached ap_percent_by_rank EXACTLY for all 5 ranks
verification_against_cached_leveling_row.quadratic_term: 0.12*0.65 gives the 7.8%AP piece and 0.0002*base gives the 1.4/2.0/2.6/3.2/3.8 %AP piece; their sum reproduces the cached row, which pins the decomposition uniquely
verification_against_cached_leveling_row.total_mixed_check: magic + true at rank 1 = 78.4 + 74.2%AP  -> matches the cached 'Total Mixed Damage' row EXACTLY

independent_computation.conclusion: The W at >=60 splinters produces two damage instances of different types. Any faithful damage_events list for this scenario must contain at least one event whose damage_type is 'true'. The only true-damage source anywhere in Syndra's kit is this W Transcendent bonus, so an event flipping magic -> true in a scenario pinned at 60 splinters is the Transcendent bonus being typed from its sourced 'Bonus True Damage' row instead of from the ability-level MAGIC_DAMAGE scalar. Typing it 'magic' understates the event by routing it through 100/(100+MR), which is the material error the old value carried.

scope_and_limits.index_resolution: The scenario definition (cast order, ranks, items, r_spheres) lives outside the permitted evidence tree, so index 4 could not be resolved to a named event directly. The verdict rests on the mechanism plus elimination: (a) at splinters=60 a true event MUST exist; (b) Syndra has exactly one true-damage source in her entire kit; (c) magic -> true is the direction of honoring the 'Bonus True Damage' row, whereas no plausible change turns a Q, E, or R-sphere event true.
scope_and_limits.residual_risk: The verdict would flip to 'both_wrong' only if the change had retyped the W's BASE recast damage to true and dropped the bonus, since the wiki's 'Total Mixed Damage' row forbids the W from being wholly true. Nothing in the permitted evidence suggests that, and such a change would also have moved the event's amount, not only its damage_type.

asides.finding: The cached quadratic modifier on both the 'Bonus True Damage' and 'Total Mixed Damage' rows is 1.14 %AP, but the correct AP^2 coefficient implied by the very same row's other two modifiers is 1.30 %AP (0.0002 * 0.65 * 100 * 100).
asides.demonstration: Rank 5 at 500 AP: closed form (0.12 + 0.0002*500) * 515 = 113.30. Reconstructing from the cached row with 1.30 gives 22.8 + 58.0 + 32.5 = 113.30 (exact); with 1.14 it gives 109.30 (short by 4.00, ~3.5%). Rank 1 at 500 AP: closed form 86.90, row@1.30 = 86.90, row@1.14 = 82.90.
asides.impact: Only matters if any consumer reads the third modifier literally instead of deriving the bonus as a multiplier on the W's magic damage. Deriving it multiplicatively (the decomposition above) is immune. Flagging as an off-task data-cache defect, consistent with CLAUDE.md's 'known-degraded wiki parses' class - note the same row's units array is the mangled '  2' string, so this row's third modifier is demonstrably a half-parse.
